positions.summary: L'Avenir en commun commits to restoring and strengthening the ISF, adding a climate component. La Facture 2027 (May 2026) confirms this is still the line.
positions.nuance: The primary text is the 2022 AEC edition; La Facture 2027 (May 2026) shows the measure carried into the 2027 programme. The chapter pages of the 2025 AEC edition on melenchon2027.fr returned 404.

positions.summary: LFI backs the Zucman tax (a 2% floor tax on fortunes above EUR 100m). The left-wide bill passed the Assemblée on 20 Feb 2025, and the tax was rejected as a budget amendment on 31 Oct 2025.
positions.nuance: The draft cited La Facture 2027 for this claim, but that page does not mention Zucman, so the source was replaced. The support is LFI's group position; the group's own roll-call vote and a personal Mélenchon quote were not opened. LFI's ISF proposal goes further than Zucman.

positions.summary: LFI conditions state aid to firms on social and ecological goals and taxes superprofits; it does not propose cutting production taxes or employer contributions.
positions.nuance: No direct statement on production taxes or employer contributions was found; the code is inferred from the programme's orientation.

positions.summary: The programme calls for 'protectionnisme écologique et solidaire': tariffs on ecological criteria, emergency anti-dumping measures for strategic industries, and a kilometre tax at the borders.
positions.nuance: The tariffs are framed around ecological criteria and strategic industries rather than classic sector quotas. The price-rise trade-off is not addressed. 2022 edition.

positions.summary: The programme would reverse privatisations, explicitly including motorways and airports, and 2026 summaries list nationalising EDF, ADP and mutual banks.
positions.nuance: Motorways are now confirmed in the primary programme text.

positions.summary: LFI would raise inheritance tax on the largest estates and cap inheritance at about EUR 12m. That is the opposite of a general cut.
positions.nuance: La Facture (2026) mentions a succession reform that favours modest transfers, so relief at the bottom is possible. The overall direction is still higher taxes.

positions.summary: Retirement at 60 after 40 years of contributions is a flagship measure, still listed in 2026.
positions.nuance: This goes beyond 62. The draft's melenchon2027.fr/programme/decouvrir page is only a landing page and does not contain the quoted measure, so it was replaced.

positions.summary: Opposes any rise in the retirement age and wants to return to 60.
positions.nuance: The programme funds pensions by raising contributions, not by raising the age.

positions.summary: LFI defends pay-as-you-go pensions, funded by higher contributions; it does not propose capitalisation.
positions.nuance: No explicit statement rejecting a funded component was found; the code rests on the long-standing LFI line.

positions.summary: Rejects debt-driven austerity ('refuser le chantage') and says it would disobey EU rules that block the programme.
positions.nuance: The draft's melenchon2027.fr/plans-2022/europe/ URL returns 404 and was replaced. The draft's claim that La Grande Conversation reported a Sept 2026 debt-cancellation plan was removed, because that article (19 Aug 2026) is about foreign policy only.

positions.summary: The programme proposes hiring more civil servants (e.g. in justice) and raising their pay; it has no plan to cut their numbers.
positions.nuance: 2022 edition.

positions.summary: Calls public debt a pretext for austerity, wants the ECB to convert the state debt it holds into perpetual zero-rate debt, and backs heavy public investment and services.
positions.nuance: The draft's only source (La Grande Conversation) contains nothing about debt and was removed, along with the unverified Banque de France claim. The programme treats debt as no obstacle rather than saying 'more debt' outright.

positions.summary: LFI opposes deficit rules and austerity, so it would oppose a constitutional golden rule.
positions.nuance: No source was opened that addresses a constitutional golden rule directly; the code rests on the party line and the anti-austerity programme (see fin1).

positions.summary: SMIC at EUR 1,600 net from day one in the 2027 version, up from EUR 1,400 net in 2022.
positions.nuance: The figure rose from EUR 1,400 (2022) to EUR 1,600 (2027 summaries).

positions.summary: The programme would restore 'protective' unemployment insurance, reverse the Macron reforms and pay benefits from the first day.
positions.nuance: 2022 edition; it also removes the obligation to accept a 'reasonable job offer'.

positions.summary: LFI opposed the 2023 'plein emploi' law that created the 15-20 hours of RSA activity. Its programme proposes an income guarantee at the poverty line. No explicit promise to abolish the hours requirement was verified.
positions.nuance: Under the brief, -2 requires a promise to abolish the obligation, and none was found. The programme predates the 2023 law and says nothing about activity conditions. LFI's vote against the law was not verified against a roll-call this session. Hence -1 (opposed, no confirmed abolition pledge).

positions.summary: The programme restores the 35-hour week, moves arduous and night work to 32 hours, and pushes to generalise 32 hours through collective bargaining.
positions.nuance: This is the 2022 edition; it was not confirmed in the 2026 summaries. Generalisation goes through negotiation rather than a legal 32-hour week.

positions.summary: The programme would make visas easier to get, regularise many undocumented people and make the 10-year residence card the standard permit. It refuses numerical caps on legal immigration.
positions.nuance: 2022 edition; MonVote2027 (2026) is consistent with it.

positions.summary: Backs a citizen-initiated referendum (RIC) on any subject but does not propose a referendum on immigration and rejects restrictive immigration agendas.
positions.nuance: No direct statement on an immigration referendum was found. A RIC could in principle allow one.

positions.summary: LFI opposes any removal or restriction of the AME.
positions.nuance: MonVote2027 cites an article dated 2025-11-06; the primary vote was not opened.

positions.summary: The programme would regularise undocumented workers, students and parents of schooled children.
positions.nuance: Broader than labour-shortage occupations.

positions.summary: LFI rejects national preference and defends universal equality of rights.
positions.nuance: No explicit mention of social housing priority; the code rests on the universalist principle and the party line.

positions.summary: The programme guarantees full droit du sol for every child born in France.
positions.nuance: 2022 edition.

positions.summary: The programme gives foreign residents the right to vote in local elections.
positions.nuance: The draft said this was limited to residents in a regular situation, but neither source states that limit.

positions.summary: LFI opposes minimum sentences (peines planchers) and focuses on prison overcrowding and reintegration.
positions.nuance: The aggregator attributes this to an Assemblée vote of 2024-09-17, but that roll call could not be verified. Evidence type was downgraded from vote to party_line.

positions.summary: LFI opposes trying minors as adults and wants more juvenile protection staff (PJJ).
positions.nuance: No source opened on this exact point; party line. The programme only mentions recruiting PJJ staff.

positions.summary: The programme would abolish the IGPN and IGGN and replace them with an independent authority attached to the Défenseur des droits.
positions.nuance: MonVote2027 indicates the measure remains in the 2025 programme.

positions.summary: Legalise recreational cannabis and regulate it through a state monopoly.
positions.nuance: Sources date from 2021-2022. A 2026 summary (TestPolitique) says 'dépénalisation', but no newer reversal was found.

positions.summary: The programme would ban all facial recognition in public spaces, including experiments.
positions.nuance: Facial recognition is a subset of AI video surveillance; the broader opposition is party line.

positions.summary: The programme would reaffirm that the constitution's fundamental principles override EU law, and apply a non-regression rule against EU norms that are less ambitious.
positions.nuance: This applies to constitutional principles and social or ecological non-regression, not blanket primacy of all French law, hence +1. The draft's 404 URL was replaced.

positions.summary: No evidence found on EU joint borrowing.
positions.nuance: The draft coded 0 with no source. Under the coding rules, 0 means explicitly mixed, so the absence of evidence must be coded null.

positions.summary: The programme makes France's EU budget contribution conditional and treats it as a lever in negotiations.
positions.nuance: This is conditional leverage, not an outright commitment to cut, hence +1. 2022 edition.

positions.summary: The programme relies on France's veto as a lever, which implies keeping unanimity.
positions.nuance: The veto passage concerns trade and enlargement, not foreign policy specifically, so the code is inferred.

positions.summary: The programme sets out an explicit strategy of disobeying EU rules that block it.
positions.nuance: The draft's melenchon2027.fr/plans-2022/europe/ URL returns 404 and was replaced.

positions.summary: The strategy is to stay in the EU: negotiate treaty change while disobeying blocking rules, then put any deal to a referendum. Leaving is not proposed.
positions.nuance: No explicit 'we will not leave' quote was opened, so -1 is kept. The 2017 'plan B' exit option does not appear in the 2022 text. The draft's 404 URL was replaced.

positions.summary: In March 2024 LFI voted against the France-Ukraine security accord, which included up to 3bn euros of military aid. Mélenchon regretted EU arms deliveries in 2022, calling them co-belligerence. The 2027 programme focuses on a diplomatic framework for a ceasefire and says nothing about military aid.
positions.nuance: No explicit 2025-2026 statement against arms deliveries was found. The 2024 vote was a non-binding Article 50-1 consultation. The 2027 programme is silent on aid, so -2 rests on 2022-2024 evidence and confidence is lowered to medium.

positions.summary: He would accept interposition troops only under UN authority and UN military command, and opposes a NATO or coalition-of-the-willing deployment.
positions.nuance: His openness to a UN force is conditional, and he rejects the French/European format the statement implies. Coded -1 rather than 0.

positions.summary: The programme calls for leaving NATO's integrated command immediately, then the organisation itself in stages.
positions.nuance: Consistent with L'Avenir en commun 2022.

positions.summary: The programme calls for sanctions on the Netanyahu government, ending economic cooperation agreements with Israel and an arms embargo. LFI also backed a European Citizens' Initiative to suspend the EU-Israel association agreement.
positions.nuance: The position is well established in both the programme and recent statements.

positions.summary: No explicit position on a 3% target was found. The programme prioritises a public arms sector and non-alignment. He has asked whether war debt is a subsidy to capitalism.
positions.nuance: The programme sets no spending figure. -1 is an inference, so confidence is low.

positions.summary: The programme creates a compulsory nine-month citizen service ('conscription citoyenne') for under-25s, paid at the SMIC. Military service is an optional part of that compulsory service.
positions.nuance: The statement says 'military OR national' service. He backs a compulsory national service in which the military part is optional, which is a full form of the statement.

positions.summary: In 2022 he questioned sanctions such as the SWIFT exclusion and called for negotiation. The 2027 programme seeks a ceasefire and the withdrawal of Russian troops. No explicit statement on lifting sanctions step by step for peace was found.
positions.nuance: Evidence is mixed and old, so the code is 0 with low confidence.

positions.summary: The 2027 programme calls for a moratorium on ZFE in their current, socially unequal design. On 28 May 2025 the LFI group voted with LR, RN and UDR for the article abolishing ZFE.
positions.nuance: The group vote for abolition points to +2, but the newer programme speaks of a moratorium and redesign. Coded +1 on the current programme.

positions.summary: The programme bans the most dangerous pesticides (glyphosate, neonicotinoids) immediately. The summary says it also bans imports of products containing them.
positions.nuance: The ban is unilateral and not conditional on foreign competitors, which matches the statement.

positions.summary: The 2027 programme has no 2035 end-of-sales position. It focuses on limiting SUVs and building light electric vehicles in France.
positions.nuance: A fetch of the climate chapter found no '2035' or 'thermique' vehicle measure. The search budget was exhausted, so EP group votes were not checked.

positions.summary: The programme ends kerosene tax exemptions and abolishes flights where a train alternative takes under four hours.
positions.nuance: The kerosene measure is framed around e-commerce dumping. No private-jet tax was found in the summary. The short-flight measure is a ban rather than a tax.

positions.summary: The programme rests on ecological planning and a constitutional 'règle verte': take no more from nature than it can rebuild.
positions.nuance: The programme does not explicitly rank climate above growth. The ranking is read from the règle verte, which as a constitutional rule overrides growth.

positions.summary: The programme exits nuclear and abandons EPR projects.
positions.nuance: Some LFI figures are pro-nuclear internally.

positions.summary: The programme exits nuclear and plans the dismantling and conversion of nuclear sites.
positions.nuance: The phase-out is planned, which matches 'progressivement'.

positions.summary: The programme includes an emergency plan for offshore wind and secures the industry's development.
positions.nuance: No onshore-wind measure was found, but nothing suggests halting wind.

positions.summary: The programme cancels liberalisation of the electricity and gas market, renationalises EDF and Engie, and restores regulated tariffs based on production costs.
positions.nuance: The summary never says 'leave the European electricity market' explicitly. The draft's 'disobey EU rules' wording was not found in the programme. National cost-based pricing is the substance of the statement, so the code stays +2 at medium confidence.

positions.summary: The programme convenes a Constituante for a Sixth Republic with 'un régime parlementaire stable'.
positions.nuance: The parliamentary character is explicit in the programme.

positions.summary: The programme elects the National Assembly by proportional representation.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme creates a RIC that can recall elected officials, propose or repeal laws, and amend the Constitution.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme's RIC can propose or repeal any law, and referendums become compulsory for constitutional changes and new EU treaties. No explicit endorsement of referendums on immigration or justice was found.
positions.nuance: A general-purpose RIC implicitly reaches these topics, but the statement echoes a right-wing proposal on immigration that LFI does not back as such.

positions.summary: The programme abolishes forced-vote procedures such as Article 49.3.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme would write into the Constitution the right to die with dignity, including with assistance. That goes further than keeping the 2026 law.
positions.nuance: The 2026 votes were free votes in every group (French Wikipedia, XVIIe législature article), so no group-line vote is claimed. The section URL slug for section 56 is inferred from the site's pattern; the text itself was read from laec.fr section 56.

positions.summary: LFI opposes restrictions on the veil in public space. The programme stresses freedom of conscience and contains no veil ban.
positions.nuance: No direct statement on a general veil ban was opened this session. The code rests on the well-known party line, so confidence is low.

positions.summary: LFI defines secularism as binding the state, not users, and warns against using it to single out Muslims. It opposes banning religious symbols for parents on school trips.
positions.nuance: The programme has no specific measure on parents accompanying school trips. The code rests on LFI's general secularism line and its known opposition to such amendments, which was not re-verified live. Low confidence.

positions.summary: LFI's laïcité centres on state neutrality and freedom of conscience. The programme pairs freedom of conscience with 'strict' laïcité aimed at state funding of religion.
positions.nuance: 'Strict' laïcité in the programme targets the state, for example no public money for religious buildings, not citizens' expression. No direct statement was opened.

positions.summary: The programme explicitly rejects surrogacy (GPA) and puts the best interest of the child first.
positions.nuance: The refusal is unqualified, so it also covers non-commercial GPA.

positions.summary: The programme suspends the school-uniform experiment.
positions.nuance: Ending even the experiment is clear opposition to making uniforms mandatory.

positions.summary: The programme cuts class sizes everywhere to beat the European average of 19 pupils, with systematic teacher hiring.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme ends ability groups in collège and keeps mixed-ability classes.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme applies a malus to public funding of contracted private schools that contribute to social segregation, and repeals the loi Carle.
positions.nuance: Nearly a word-for-word match with the statement.

positions.summary: A key programme measure guarantees every holder of the baccalauréat access to the course of their choice without selection, by dismantling Parcoursup. The 2025 edition keeps the abolition of Parcoursup.
positions.nuance: The phrase 'sans sélection' is explicit, so the -2 or +2 split note in the brief is satisfied: this is not merely replacing the platform.

positions.summary: The programme regulates where doctors may set up practice, makes on-call duty compulsory and recruits salaried public doctors for under-served areas.
positions.nuance: Regulating where doctors set up is a constraint on new doctors, but not explicitly a requirement to serve a few years in under-served areas. Coded +1 for this partial support.

positions.summary: The programme repeals the 2024 rise in medical co-payments and aims for '100% Sécu' coverage.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme caps rents everywhere in France and lowers them in big cities.
positions.nuance: This goes further than the statement, which covers only shortage areas.

positions.summary: The programme renationalises SNCF and refuses tendering of rail lines. It cancels energy-market liberalisation and renationalises EDF and Engie.
positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme goes the other way from 'social VAT'. It cuts VAT on essential goods and funds this with a 'TVA grand luxe'. No general VAT increase is proposed.
positions.nuance: No explicit statement on 'TVA sociale' was found. The code is inferred from a programme measure that runs the opposite way (lower VAT on essentials, funded by taxing luxury goods). The source is the 2022 edition: the 2025 edition chapters could not be retrieved, because melenchon2027.fr chapter URLs return 404. Low confidence.

positions.summary: The programme explicitly promises to facilitate access to French nationality, alongside full birthright citizenship and the regularisation of workers.
positions.nuance: The measure covers access to nationality in general, which includes naturalising long-term legal residents. The source is the 2022 edition; the 2025 text could not be retrieved.

positions.summary: The programme explicitly includes an identity-check receipt to fight ethnic profiling, with training, monitoring and sanctions.
positions.nuance: Verbatim measure from the 2022 edition. The draft's claim about LFI bills was not verified and has been dropped. No sign of a reversal, but the 2025 edition text could not be retrieved, so confidence is medium.

positions.summary: The programme calls for leaving NATO and building an 'independent, republican and popular' national defence. It gives priority to buying French military equipment and to public ownership of the arms industry, which is the opposite of pooled European defence.
positions.nuance: The programme does not mention a 'European army' by name. The code rests on its sovereign-defence and national-procurement line, which conflicts directly with giving up military autonomy. The source is the 2022 edition; no 2025-2026 statement was retrieved.

positions.summary: The programme would use France's veto to block any new EU enlargement without prior social, fiscal and environmental harmonisation. That is conditional opposition, which would apply to Ukraine's accession.
positions.nuance: This is a general condition on enlargement, not a statement about Ukraine specifically. No 2025-2026 statement by Mélenchon on Ukraine's accession was retrieved. If he has since opposed it outright, the code would be -2.

positions.summary: The programme explicitly guarantees farmers remunerative prices through floor prices and bans sales at a loss.
positions.nuance: Verbatim from the 2022 edition. This is a long-standing LFI demand and there is no sign of a reversal.

positions.summary: The programme cuts VAT on essential goods and freezes the prices of basic necessities. No specific 5.5% VAT rate on electricity, gas and fuels was found.
positions.nuance: Partial support, inferred: whether energy counts as an 'essential product' is not stated. The draft's claim that LFI is wary of subsidising fuel was unsourced and has been removed. Not verified for 2025-2026.

positions.summary: LFI defends public broadcasting. Its programme keeps France Télévisions and Radio France public, with their presidents elected by Parliament, and nothing in it points toward privatisation.
positions.nuance: The programme assumes public ownership but contains no explicit anti-privatisation pledge. LFI's votes against the 2025 holding-company reform were not verified this session.

positions.summary: LFI opposes extending bans on religious symbols to university students, consistent with its view that secularism binds the state, not users.
positions.nuance: No university-specific statement was retrieved. Inferred from the programme's secularism doctrine and the party line. Low confidence.

positions.summary: The programme pledges to fight the artificialisation of land and to build public housing to the most ambitious ecological standards. Both run directly against loosening building rules and the ZAN target.
positions.nuance: The source is the 2022 edition. LFI's votes on the 2025-2026 bills loosening ZAN were not verified this session.

record.bio: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a French politician born in 1951. He spent about thirty years in the Socialist Party, serving as senator for Essonne and as junior minister for vocational education (2000-2002), left the PS in 2008 to co-found the Parti de Gauche, and founded La France insoumise (LFI) in 2016. He was an MEP from 2009 to 2017 and deputy for Bouches-du-Rhône from 2017 to 2022, and ran for president in 2012 (fourth), 2017 (fourth) and 2022 (third). On 3 May 2026 he announced a fourth candidacy for 2027, built on an updated L'Avenir en commun and a Sixth Republic via a constituent assembly.
offices: Conseiller général de l'Essonne and président délégué du conseil général (not president)
Ministre délégué à l'Enseignement professionnel (gouvernement Jospin), 27 March 2000 - 6 May 2002
Président du groupe LFI à l'Assemblée nationale
Co-founder of the Parti de Gauche (2008); founder and leader of La France insoumise
legal: Rebellion, provocation and intimidation of judicial authority during the 16 October 2018 searches of LFI headquarters: tried in Bobigny on 19-20 September 2019 and sentenced on 9 December 2019 to 3 months' suspended imprisonment and an 8,000 EUR fine. He did not appeal, so the conviction is final.

European Parliament assistants affair (suspected use of EP-paid assistants for the Parti de Gauche, 2009-2017; preliminary inquiry July 2017, judicial investigation from November 2018). Investigating judges closed the instruction on 26 May 2026 without placing Mélenchon under formal investigation (no mise en examen). Two former assistants were témoins assistés. Telos reports that no evidence established his direct involvement or an organised scheme. No formal non-lieu order was located in this check, but with no one mis en examen no trial can follow.

reversals.before: 1992: called for a yes vote on the Maastricht treaty, calling it a 'compromis de gauche' and presenting the single currency as an instrument of European civilisation.
reversals.after: Campaigned against the 2005 constitutional treaty and later said 'ce sont les opposants à ce traité qui avaient raison'. Now proposes 'Plan A / Plan B' (renegotiate the treaties or disobey them), described as 'ni Frexit, ni Europe libérale'.

reversals.before: 2014: called the annexation of Crimea 'absolutely predictable' and opposed sanctions on Russia.
reversals.after: February 2022: condemned the Russian invasion while still assigning NATO a share of responsibility; by June 2022 he endorsed arms deliveries, affirming Ukraine's right to defend itself, while opposing deeper French military involvement.

delivery.what: Junior minister for vocational education (2000-2002): reformed vocational aptitude certificates (CAP) and the validation of acquired experience (validation des acquis), and created the 'lycée des métiers' label.
delivery.assessment: Encyclopedic sources credit him with concrete reforms in a junior portfolio. The record is short (about two years) and dated, and no sources of other leanings were consulted on its impact.

delivery.what: Led the LFI group in the Assemblée nationale (June 2017 - October 2021) and built the NUPES left alliance for the 2022 legislative elections (131 seats per French Wikipedia; totals vary with how allied deputies are counted). LFI later took part in the 2024 Nouveau Front populaire, which won a relative majority; LFI proposed his name for Matignon, but the other coalition partners rejected it.
delivery.assessment: A significant coalition-building and opposition record, though he gained no executive power. Roll-call votes were not checked.

delivery.what: 2027 programme (updated L'Avenir en commun): net SMIC of 1,600 EUR, retirement at 60 after 40 years of contributions, price freezes on essential goods and energy, a strengthened wealth tax (ISF), a Sixth Republic via a constituent assembly, and a nuclear exit by 2050.
delivery.assessment: These are promises only, taken from a secondary aggregator summary and not from the primary programme text. Costings are disputed, and that dispute was not verified here.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not directly sampled in this check. LFI and sympathetic outlets present him as the main voice of social rupture and ecological planning, and present the judicial cases as political harassment. After the May 2026 closure, LFI said that no investigating judge had found grounds for a mise en examen.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets (JDD, CNews) cover him largely through his legal cases and the 2018 searches. They reported the May 2026 closure of the assistants investigation without indictment.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Neutral and encyclopedic sources (Wikipedia, Telos, L'Essentiel) describe a left-wing leader with a long PS career. They mention both his oratorical talent and controversies over provocative statements, and report that he was never charged in the EP assistants case.
